//: Story Phase 6, chapter 30: The Mightiest Gust Yet. The biggest set-piece so far (screen shake and flashes follow the accessibility settings). The ship inflates; gas jets from every seam ('The wood is breathing!'); a new, sharper profile (rotten garlic, onion, Frog Grog, a cheese finish); the pressure sets off every loaded cannon, one by one, into empty sea ('WE'RE PIRATES!'; nobody hurt, nothing hit). Then the smell. The Second Yellow Apocalypse: a new Dead Center (generation 2: still ONE lethal zone, garlic-pale). The release goes through the hull into the water and the sharks go mad; then they start going round. The Great Sharkstorm forms, and Garrick names it.
p6c6.begin: A tiny vibration. Somewhere, a teacup rattles in its saucer.
BWOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOMMMMMMMMMMMM.
The deck jumps. The lanterns leap on their hooks. Barrels roll. Hammocks below swing up and hit the beams. Every dish aboard breaks at once.
The mast bends like a fishing rod. The rigging goes as tight as harp strings. Half the crew are knocked flat; the other half were already lying down on purpose.
The Grand Stenchmaster's cape flies straight out behind him, horizontal, flapping. His medals stand out on their ribbons.
And the ship...
...the ship INFLATES.
The deck lifts. The hull bulges outward between the ribs. Planks creak out of true. Nails sing as they pull.
captain[alarmed]: She's going to BURST!
Then the gas finds the way out: every seam, every porthole, every crack in the timber. Yellow jets spray from both sides of the hull at once.
The ship itself appears to be farting.
pete[alarmed]: The WOOD is BREATHING!
gristle[alarmed]: It should NOT be doing that!
BOOM. The pressure kicks a cannon off its wedge, and it fires.
BOOM.
BOOM BOOM BOOM BOOM. The whole broadside goes off down the starboard side, one gun after another, each trailing a little ribbon of yellow fume into the dark.
captain[alarmed]: WHY ARE THE CANNONS LOADED?
crew: WE'RE PIRATES!
Far out in the dark, eight splashes. There is nothing out there to hit. There is, thankfully, nobody out there to see.
Slowly, groaning, the Revenge lets out the last of the breath she never meant to take, and settles back into her own shape. Mostly.
Silence. A plank somewhere drops on the deck.
garrick[relieved]: ...Now THAT was a proper Grand Stenchmaster event.
Nobody answers him.
Then the smell hits.
p6c6.apocalypse: It is not the old smell.

It is rotten garlic, sharp as a knife. It is raw onion. It is Frog Grog, for body. And underneath it all, slowly arriving, like a guest nobody invited, something like a cheese that has been kept in a boot.
Eyes water all over the deck. Pete's eyebrows try to leave.
garrick[proud]: Notes of aged garlic. A bright onion top. The Frog Grog gives it body. And a cheese finish. That's from Tuesday.
quill[coughing]: We don't want the TASTING PROFILE!
Squawks puts his head out of your coat, takes one sniff, and goes rigid.
You pull the coat over him and turn your back to it.

Forward, the cloud is settling. It's paler than the old one, a sick, glowing, garlic yellow, and it seems to shimmer at the edges like heat over a road. Where the old Center was, there is nothing: the new one has eaten it, and taken its place.
garrick[businesslike]: It'll drift to the stern.
garrick[businesslike]: Port, then. As I said.
It rises, slowly, up the foremast.
garrick[smug]: Upward. Which I also said.

p6c6.apocalypse.tutorial: Get aft, clear of the new cloud (by the cabin door).
p6c6.apocalypse.title: The Second Yellow Apocalypse

p6c6.clear: You make the cabin door with half the crew. The new cloud hangs over the forward deck and glows, faintly, like something radioactive in a story.
You set the basket down in the lee of the cabin door.
p6c6.check: captain[tender]: Ye haven't got any. Nothing to take.
Over the rail, the water has started to make a noise you've never heard water make.
p6c6.frenzy: You go to the rail and look over.
The release went through the hull. Through the planks, through the seams, out into the sea all round the ship in a great glowing yellow bloom.
Fins everywhere, packed so close they clatter together. Water boiling white. Jaws snapping at bubbles. One shark is trying to eat a plank. Another shark is trying to eat the first shark.
captain[angry]: This is not market research.
Then, all at once, the snapping stops.
The fins begin to move together. Round the ship. All in the same direction.
Faster. Tighter. The water follows them, turning, turning, until the whole sea round the Revenge is going round like soup being stirred.
A whirlpool. Spray flies off it, yellow with fume. The first shark lifts out of the water, spinning, surprised.
A column rises out of the sea, turning: water and spray and timber and yellow fume and sharks, sharks, sharks, all going round, all the way up into the cloud.
Lightning cracks down the middle of it.
garrick[proud]: THE GRAND STENCHMASTER'S GREAT SHARKSTORM!
